name: DFPlayer Mini MP3 player
description: Serial MP3/WAV player that plays numbered files from a micro SD card (FAT16/FAT32, up to 32 GB) and drives a speaker under 3 W directly (or headphones / an amplifier from DAC_L/DAC_R). Controlled at 9600 baud with 10-byte frames (0x7E FF 06 CMD FB MSB LSB, 16-bit checksum = minus the sum of the 6 middle bytes, 0xEF); query commands return volume, track count, current track and play state. Supply 3.2-5.0 V, 3.3 V logic. Sold as: DFRobot DFPlayer Mini MP3 player (DFR0299, and the many same-pinout clone modules), 16 pins in two rows: VCC RX TX DAC_R DAC_L SPK_1 GND SPK_2, opposite side bottom to top IO_1 GND IO_2 ADKEY_1 ADKEY_2 USB+ USB- BUSY.
eli5: A tiny music box: put MP3 files on a memory card, plug in a speaker, and your board tells it which song to play and how loud.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 3.2-5.0 V (typ. 4.2 V; 5 V gives the most speaker power)

pins.name: RX
pins.description: Module serial input (3.3 V TTL): wire to the board's UART TX, through a 1 kOhm resistor

pins.name: TX
pins.description: Module serial output (3.3 V TTL, 9600 baud): wire to the board's UART RX

pins.name: DAC_R
pins.description: Line/headphone audio out, right channel (to an amplifier or earphone)

pins.name: DAC_L
pins.description: Line/headphone audio out, left channel (to an amplifier or earphone)

pins.name: SPK_1
pins.description: Speaker output (mono, under 3 W, 4-8 Ohm), to one speaker wire; never connect to ground

pins.name: SPK_2
pins.description: Speaker output, to the other speaker wire; never connect to ground

pins.name: IO_1
pins.description: Button input to GND: short press = previous track, long press = volume down

pins.name: IO_2
pins.description: Button input to GND: short press = next track, long press = volume up

pins.name: USB+
pins.description: USB D+ for a USB flash drive or PC

pins.name: USB-
pins.description: USB D- for a USB flash drive or PC

pins.name: BUSY
pins.description: Play status output: low while playing, high when idle (3.3 V level)

supplierQuery: DFPlayer Mini MP3 player module micro SD
buildNotes: Cross the serial wires: module TX -> board RX, board TX -> 1 kOhm resistor -> module RX (DFRobot's fix for noise and 5 V boards). 9600 baud 8N1.
Power from 5 V with a 100 uF+ capacitor across VCC/GND near the module: speaker peaks cause resets and clicks on a weak supply. The module draws under 15 mA idle, far more when driving a speaker.
A speaker (under 3 W, 4-8 Ohm) goes between SPK_1 and SPK_2; never tie either to GND. For headphones or an external amplifier use DAC_L/DAC_R with GND.
After power-on wait 0.5-1.5 s (the module sends 7E FF 06 3F ... when ready); commands sent earlier are ignored.

Frames are 7E FF 06 CMD FB MSB LSB CHK_H CHK_L EF; checksum = 0x10000 - (sum of the 6 bytes after 0x7E). Query commands (0x42 status, 0x43 volume, 0x48 SD track count, 0x4C current SD track) reply with the same CMD and the value in MSB/LSB.

Track numbers follow the order files were copied to the card, not their names: copy 0001.mp3, 0002.mp3... in order, or use folders 01-99 with 001.mp3-255.mp3 (command 0x0F) or a folder named MP3 with 0001.mp3... (command 0x12).
BUSY is low while a track plays; read it with a GPIO instead of polling the status query if you want.
In the simulator the query replies come from the sliders (SD track count, volume, current track, play state, EQ); playback commands are accepted but do not move the sliders.

sim.quantity: Tracks in the SD card root

controls.quantity: EQ (0 Normal, 1 Pop, 2 Rock, 3 Jazz, 4 Classic, 5 Bass)

example.code:
from machine import UART, Pin
import time
from dfplayer import DFPlayer

uart = UART({UART_ID}, baudrate=9600, tx=Pin({RX}), rx=Pin({TX}))
time.sleep_ms(1500)  # the module needs up to 1.5 s to read the card after power-on
df = DFPlayer(uart)
names = ('stopped', 'playing', 'paused')
while True:
    dev, st = df.status()
    print('FILES=%d VOL=%d TRACK=%d %s' % (df.sd_track_count(), df.volume(), df.current_sd_track(), names[st] if st < 3 else '?'))
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: Reports the SD track count, volume, current track and play state set on the sliders
